questions.question: Explain how curiosity encouraged European exploration.
questions.expected_answer: Renaissance ideas encouraged people to ask questions and find out for themselves. Europeans knew little about much of the world, and mapmakers and rulers wanted to fill in the empty spaces on their maps and know how far Africa stretched. Sailors had fears of boiling seas and monsters, but voyages such as Gil Eanes sailing past Cape Bojador in 1434 showed these fears were wrong. Prince Henry the Navigator organised and paid for many early voyages.

questions.question: Explain why spices were so expensive in Europe and why this encouraged exploration.
questions.expected_answer: Spices came from India, Sri Lanka and the islands of what is now Indonesia along long overland and sea routes, passing through many Indian, Arab, Persian, Turkish and Venetian traders who each added a profit, and rulers charged taxes. After the Ottomans captured Constantinople in 1453, they controlled many routes. A sea route around Africa would let Portugal buy spices directly and make huge profits.

questions.question: Apart from spices, what did the Portuguese seek in Africa, and what were the consequences?
questions.expected_answer: The Portuguese traded for gold from West African kingdoms and built the fortress of Elmina in 1482 in what is now Ghana. The search for profit also led them, from the 1440s, to capture and buy African people as enslaved workers, which grew into the transatlantic slave trade that caused enormous suffering to millions of Africans.
